core_obligations: Implications (3) -> (2) -> (1) are immediate from the definitions.

(1) implies (4): Y^nu -> Y is finite by the alteration lemma; factor X -> Y^nu; the factorization is finite over the open V containing all codimension at most 1 points, flat over V since a normal local ring of dimension at most 2 is Cohen-Macaulay, and V is regular by descent-regular; the complement of V is a finite set of singular points.

For each singular point the base change to the henselian local ring O_{Y^nu, y_i}^h is a regular alteration (the verification that the alteration property carries to the henselian base is the omitted detail and is carried as a core obligation); by the local alteration lemma (published item 737, declared external) the completion of O_{Y^nu, y_i}^h is normal.

(4) implies (3): replace Y by its normalization; choose elementary etale neighbourhoods at the singular points; the henselian local rings there have isomorphic completions, so the scheme-case resolution theorem gives normalized blowup sequences on the neighbourhoods; assemble a global sequence through the sequence-equivalence lemma and observe X_n is regular by looking at local rings.
proof_roadmap: Immediate implications; normalization finiteness and codimension-1 flatness for (1) -> (4); henselian base alteration check (omitted in source); scheme-case resolution and sequence assembly for (4) -> (3).
difficulty_reason: The main theorem assembles four equivalences: the (1) -> (4) chain stacks finiteness, flatness and descent lemmas, and the (4) -> (3) chain imports the scheme theorem through henselian completions and the sequence-equivalence lemma; both directions are multi-step constructions.
